newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Southern African leaders to meet private sector.
newsitem.headline: Southern African leaders to meet private sector.

text.p: The leaders of 12 southern African countries will meet the private sector in Botswana in May to promote cooperation in the area of development, a statement from the Botswana government said.

The first Southern Africa International Dialogue on Smart Partnership will be held at the Botswana tourist centre in Kasane between May 4 and 7, the office of President Ketumile Masire of Botswana said at the weekend.
The conference will be attended by presidents Masire, Bakili Muluzi of Malawi, Sam Nujoma of Namibia and Zimbabwe's Robert Mugabe.

It will be chaired by newly elected Bank of Botswana governor, Baledzi Gaolathe, currently managing director of Debswana Diamond Company, and Cyril Ramaphosa, deputy executive chairman of South Africa's New Africa Investments Limited (NAIL).
Business and government will exchange views on tranforming southern Africa into a growth centre in the global economic environment.
Private sector leaders from Paraguay, Jordan, Cyprus, Malta, the Britain, Canada and New Zealand will also participate.
